MCH.title: The Machine Consciousness Hypothesis
MCH.date_label: Revised January 15, 2026; document first dated September 15, 2025
MCH.date_boundary: These passages are bound to the captured January 2026 revision, not silently assigned to the September 2025 version.

A11.plain: A representation is an implemented pattern interpreted through a suitable mechanism.
A11.limit: Structural invariances characterize representations; this is not a theorem that all transformations preserve them.

A12.plain: Communicating cells are proposed to organize coherent models and agentic control.
A12.limit: The developmental Genesis hypothesis and consciousness-as-coherence operator are additional commitments.

A13.plain: Conscious model-building is connected to planning and control of action.
A13.limit: This is not an experimentally demonstrated cellular action-selection algorithm.

A14.plain: Present experience includes represented content and a sense of its current occurrence.
A14.limit: Realness is a representational feature, not a tonic-baseline measurement.

A15.plain: Representations propagate and transform through a causal processing network.
A15.limit: The paper does not specify every operator as a SAN phase-wave mechanism.

A16.plain: Artificial self-organizing systems are proposed as tests of biological consciousness hypotheses.
A16.limit: Pages 22 and 24 explicitly leave successful artificial reproduction and consciousness uncertain.

CIMC.title: CIMC Research Program Whitepaper
CIMC.date_boundary: The current capture differs from the archived V2 title-page text; extracted body text on pages 2-30 is identical. No claim of identical visual layout is made.

A11.plain: The proposed conscious organization is computational and open to implementation tests.
A11.limit: Interpretive validation is proposed; conscious implementation is not demonstrated.

A12.plain: Self-organized perception is proposed to monitor and regulate coherent internal models.
A12.limit: Same-level metarepresentation and transparency are additional representational constraints.

A13.plain: Agency selects actions using internal goals and representations.
A13.limit: Agency and consciousness are explicitly distinguished, so this match concerns an adjacent functional component.

A14.plain: Conscious experience includes present registration within an internally constructed perceptual field.
A14.limit: Minimal experience without a specified object is not identical to SAN's maintained object pattern.

A15.plain: Local updates and exchanges are proposed to organize mutually consistent representations.
A15.limit: Neural cellular automata and request-confirmation networks are research directions, not demonstrated conscious systems.

A16.plain: Different implementations may converge on corresponding solutions to a shared control problem.
A16.limit: Convergence toward consciousness is a hypothesis, not a finding that consciousness has been reproduced.

SC-A12.title: A self arises through communicating cells
SC-A12.quote: the point is that we are establishing a self communication mechanism, they listen to each other, and to any other available incoming signals
SC-A12.plain: SAN places the deciding self inside a network of cells that listen, learn, and change their connections.
chain: incoming patterns
cells receive, predict, emit and adapt communication paths
distributed learned organization participating in the deciding self
SC-A12.shared: Communicating units organize a larger system associated with self-directed behavior.
SC-A12.residual: The June source does not state the later Genesis hypothesis that consciousness is the simplest developmental prerequisite for intelligence, or a global coherence objective.

SC-A13.title: Prediction guides what happens next
SC-A13.quote: Dendrites have to recognize this hertz in order for another part of the sequence to know what it means, and another part of the sequence to predict what comes next.
SC-A13.plain: SAN links recognized signals to predictions about the next step in a distributed sequence.
chain: signals from other cells
receiver recognizes a pattern and predicts its next response
next firing or waiting step in the sequence
SC-A13.shared: An internal representation contributes to selection of a future response.
SC-A13.residual: The June source gives a cellular next-response example. It does not yet spell out the later goal-and-preference definition of organism-level agency; the November source supplies the stronger action-planning bridge.

SC-A15.title: One unit receives what another unit produces
SC-A15.quote: critically what they are learning they are rendering materially because their connections reshape themselves to create paths that represent learned patterns as paths, synaptic communication paths between cells, a short term memory mechanism.
SC-A15.plain: SAN describes learned patterns changing the paths through which cells communicate and process later signals.
chain: received pattern
local interpretation, emission and learned path change
another receiver processes the emitted pattern
SC-A15.shared: Local interpretation and updates connect processing units into a causal information-processing network.
SC-A15.residual: The cellular learning account is not a specification of every later conditional operator or request/confirmation protocol. The shared receive-update-output chain remains visible.

CP-A11.title: Experience is a constructed information pattern
CP-A11.quote: A rendering is a substantial pattern that is the output of some computable process.
CP-A11.plain: SAN treats a conscious rendering as a real information pattern produced and sustained by processing.
chain: information-bearing activity
computable processing and recurrent re-rendering
a represented pattern available inside the system
CP-A11.shared: A representation is an implemented pattern used by a computational process, not a separate observer outside that process.
CP-A11.residual: The shared computational-pattern account is not a formal proof of identical semantics or of sufficient conditions for consciousness.

CP-A12.title: The self is represented inside its own loop
CP-A12.quote: conciousness is context referencing context, self referencing self, where self is a rendered pattern that is a distinct information/energy configuration, that oscillates inside a feedback loop that is made up of brain state elements that alternately render & detect renderings,
CP-A12.plain: SAN describes the self as a pattern inside feedback between elements that produce and detect representations.
chain: distributed sensory and internal representations
recurrent rendering, detection and coordination
a self represented in relation to a world and capable of coordinated action
CP-A12.shared: The self/world organization is constructed inside a recurring representational process.
CP-A12.residual: SAN specifies oscillatory rendering and reception; the targets add particular metarepresentational and developmental conditions. These additions qualify whole-theory identity, not the shared subchain.

CP-A13.title: Imagined futures organize action
CP-A13.quote: Our decisions that arise from mental imagery, from our predictions of consequences, our predictions of possible futures, result in sparse distributed muscle coordination actions sequences
CP-A13.plain: SAN connects predictions of possible futures with coordinated action, speech, writing, and planning.
chain: mental imagery and predicted consequences
selection and coordination of distributed action patterns
movement, speech, writing and planning
CP-A13.shared: Internal models of possible outcomes participate in selecting and coordinating action.
CP-A13.residual: The November source gives a proposed oscillatory motor-coordination route. The target passages do not supply that same motor implementation or prove the two accounts mathematically equivalent.

CP-A14.title: A current experience is a maintained pattern
CP-A14.quote: the rendering in the mind is a persistent pattern that is detected by the mind the same way a rock in the world is a persistent pattern that is detectable by a computer with a neural network with a semantic segmentation program
CP-A14.plain: SAN describes a currently experienced object as a maintained internal pattern, distinct from its ongoing background.
chain: changing sensory and internal activity
repeated construction and detection of a persistent representation
currently available conscious content
CP-A14.shared: Present experience is treated as an internally represented and presently available condition.
CP-A14.residual: This is a bounded conceptual/process-prefix match. Tonic-baseline discrimination is not identical to the target definition of realness, and it does not establish the targets' minimal-content phenomenology.

CP-A15.title: Rendering is distributed across the network
CP-A15.quote: Metaphorically you can imagine that there is no central canvas, no computer screen where all the renderings show up, because the rendered outputs are distributed all over the place, and absorbed by the brain for the next iteration of the rendering.
CP-A15.plain: SAN makes each output part of the next stage of processing; no single central screen is required.
chain: a local representation
distributed transformation and reception by another processing unit
a further representation used in subsequent processing
CP-A15.shared: Representations participate in a network of local transformations rather than waiting for an external inner reader.
CP-A15.residual: No full operator-by-operator translation has been proved. Neither the SAN analogy nor the MCH text proves that every transformation preserves every structural invariant.

CP-A16.title: The proposed organization can inform artificial minds
CP-A16.quote: Beyond the electro-chemical dynamics, oscillatory physics is what binds our minds together, and the simulation of oscillatory physics is what can bind artificial minds together.
CP-A16.plain: SAN proposes carrying an organizing process from biological minds into an artificial implementation.
chain: an identified organization in biological processing
reproduce the relevant organization in an artificial system
test a functionally corresponding artificial mind
CP-A16.shared: Biological organization motivates an artificial implementation rather than making the biological material the only possible carrier.
CP-A16.residual: SAN proposes an oscillatory route. The targets explore self-organization and convergence without establishing that the same oscillatory implementation is necessary or that any implementation is conscious.

Pages 22 and 24 explicitly leave successful artificial reproduction and consciousness uncertain.
rows.formal_relation: Source-grounded partial process/functional correspondence, not a constructed functor, proven isomorphism or bisimulation.

L1.basis: Both allow functionally comparable representations across implementations and propose artificial realization. Their organizing principles and sufficiency claims are not identical.

L2.basis: A biological organizing account motivates an artificial construction program. The source proposes oscillatory physics; the target searches for self-organizing learning conditions.

L3.basis: Comparable information or agency can motivate a search for shared organization. It does not force consciousness, a unique algorithm or oscillatory implementation.
